spectrum.note: Sa and SaM by Eq 6.2.34 with R = 1, I = 1 and the 5 % spectrum (eta = 1). The MCE spectrum is 1.5 times the design spectrum (Sec 2.5.16.3.1; Eq 6.2.34's 2/3 is the DBE share of the MCE). Sec 2.5.16.2.1 prints SaM 'for period TD' though DM uses TM: the larger of Sa at TD and at TM is used (the more conservative of the printed and the evident reading).

forces.note: Minimum (1): the Sec 2.5.7 force at T = TD with I = 1.0 and R = RI ('isolated'), the more conservative of the readings, since the clause does not say which R.

spectrumAnalysis.note: dampedFromShare is SAEngine practice, not BNBC: the analysis spectrum takes the isolation damping (÷ B of the lesser of the effective damping and 30 %) from 0.8 TD up, the 5 % spectrum below, so the isolated modes take the isolation damping and the higher modes the fixed-base damping. BNBC sets the damping per mode but not how one spectrum carries it.

torsion.note: The total displacements of Sec 2.5.16.2.1: the deck above the isolators rotates rigidly about the centre of rigidity of the isolators; the eccentricity is the actual one plus the accidental share of Sec 2.5.7.6.2 (the seismic table's) of the isolators' plan extent across the motion. BNBC asks for the spatial distribution of the isolators' stiffness and the most disadvantageous eccentric mass but gives no formula.

requirements.text: Property variation over the life (ageing, contamination, moisture, temperature, creep, fatigue)
Wind above the isolation interface, and a wind restraint limiting the isolator drift to the storey drift
Fire rating of the isolators as for the columns and walls around them
No displacement restraint below the total maximum displacement
Each unit stable under the design vertical load at the total maximum displacement
Overturning at the isolation interface under the MCE
Local uplift without overstress or instability
Quality control tests of every unit before installation
Final inspection of the separations and the components crossing the interface
Periodic monitoring, inspection and maintenance programme
Work at the isolation interface under an experienced design professional

review: Site-specific seismic criteria, spectra and ground motions
Preliminary design: total design displacement and lateral force level
Final design of the whole structural system and its analyses
Quality control testing programme of the isolators
